assessment: Here is the wish engine most decks would kill for: it is your commander, it costs no card, and it never runs dry. Sisay's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation puts any legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power onto the battlefield — 3 targets at power 2, then 10, 23, 28 and 33 as your other legends add colours, and nothing in the deck costs more than five, so four colours already unlocks everything. No tap symbol, no once-per-turn clause: the only cap is producing five distinct pips again, which is why the goldfish target that matters is 'Sisay online with a five-colour mana source' — 55.8% by turn six, mean turn 4.22. The discipline is knowing what she cannot find: 26 of the 99 are non-legendary, including every counterspell, both free protection instants and half the pip battery. Fetch what only she can reach, and draw the rest.

targets.scenario: The default. Turn 4-5, two colours among your other legends — say Katilda's green and white — so Sisay is a 4/4 with a 'mana value less than 4' gate. You can pay the five pips once and nobody is pressuring you yet.
targets.why: The default wish is the one that widens the next wish. Derevi is mana value 3 and brings white, blue and green on a single card, so the ladder jumps toward the 28-and-33-target pool in one fetch. She reads as a fair 2/3, taps or untaps a permanent whenever your creatures connect — and she is the checker-verified half of the deck's kill (stack 002). You are buying access today and the loop's quiet half for later, on one unthreatening card.

targets.scenario: The fuel fetch. Three colours up, Sisay a 5/5, but you are paying the activation off lands alone — the goldfish's mean available mana at turn six is 5.87 against a five-pip cost, so a second activation per rotation is out of reach.
targets.why: Half the pip battery — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends — is non-legendary and invisible to Sisay, but Selvala is the battery piece she CAN find. Her {G} plus a tap makes X mana in any combination of colours, X being your largest creature's power: with Sisay at 5, that is the full {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} in one activation. She wakes up on your next turn — her ability taps — so this is tomorrow's second fetch bought today, with a body the table reads as ramp.

targets.scenario: The answer fetch, under pressure. Three colours up, Sisay a 5/5, and the pod has shown the shrink attack — a colour rung just ate spot removal in response to an activation.
targets.why: Mana value 4, legal under the 'less than 5' gate, and she gives you, your planeswalkers and every OTHER creature you control hexproof — every future colour rung becomes untargetable and the whole kill-the-rung attack is retired. She does not protect herself, so fetch her before you need her, not after. Sweepers and -X/-X still get through: keep a two-colour legend in hand as the rebuild.

targets.scenario: The lock-breaker. A stax seat has an artifact or enchantment squeezing your five-pip, zero-generic activation, and the strategic frame is blunt about your role here: you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion.
targets.why: The deck's only artifact-or-enchantment answer stapled to a legendary body, which makes it the only one Sisay can go and get — mana value 3, live from two colours. Her enter trigger destroys the piece that breaks the lock on YOU, not the scariest piece on the table, and her '{T}: You and target opponent each draw a card' buys goodwill afterwards. One fetch, one answer, one friend.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. The combo seat is one untap from trying it, and your counterspells are exactly where they always are — in the non-legendary blind spot, not your hand.
targets.why: Nobody expects a battlefield tutor to fetch a planeswalker hatebear, and he is legal from two colours at mana value 3. 'Each opponent can cast spells only any time they could cast a sorcery' deletes instant-speed combo and instant-speed interaction in the same breath — the closest thing this deck has to tutorable disruption, since all six counterspells are non-legendary and must be drawn. His minus-three bounce is the backup answer when the problem is already on the battlefield.

targets.scenario: The closing fetch. Derevi and two other creatures are ready to attack, and you can produce {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} twice this turn — once for the fetch, once held for combat.
targets.why: Take her on the turn she wins, not the turn she impresses. Stack 002 is your script: combat 1's activation is pre-funded from five untapped lands, combat 2 breaks even on Derevi triggers, and the first defending player dies during combat 4 — at a life cost of 0, because Command Tower covers {B} and Plaza of Heroes covers the rest, so City of Brass and Mana Confluence never tap. Until that turn she is worth more in the library: a bracket 4 table reads Najeela next to a five-colour mana base as 'they have it', and Sisay can fetch her at will.

tutors.notes: Cold starts: at power 2 the gate is 'mana value less than 2' — Mox Amber, Yoshimaru, Mikaeus, and only Yoshimaru steps the ladder. Mox Amber is colourless, and Mikaeus fetched rather than cast is an open question flagged for a stack scenario (a fetched card is not cast, so X may be 0). Land a colour-diverse legend before the first activation instead. And remember the power check happens on resolution: the fetch you announce is not always the fetch you get, so know your second choice at every rung.

gaps: The blind spot is structural: 26 of the 99 are non-legendary and outside Sisay's reach at any power — all six counterspells, both free protection instants, all four Game Changers, and three of the six pieces that can pay her activation (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends). She finds payoffs; fuel and stack-speed protection must be drawn. Two open questions gate the wish list and each needs a stack scenario before you build a turn on it: whether Mikaeus fetched arrives as a 0/0, and whether a freshly fetched legend can help pay for a second activation in the same turn.
